title: Charminar
summary: Charminar is a square monument with four minarets in Hyderabad, India, built by Sultan Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah in 1591, with construction beginning in 1589. Accounts differ on why it was built, among them marking the city foundation, honouring his wife Bhagmati or ending a plague; the Telangana district page says the reason is unclear. Quoted minaret heights are 48.7 m or 56 m.

uncertainty.note: The Telangana district page says it was built in 1591 and that construction began in 1589 and took two years; start is the completion year with a two-year lower bound. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: Charminar was built by Sultan Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah in 1591; construction began in 1589 and was completed in two years
Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah commissioned the construction in 1591

importance.justification: Landmark of Hyderabad erected to commemorate the founding of the city, per Incredible India.
